scenes.summary: From a Tethergrid interceptor position, Cyrus watches maintenance traffic continue with no launch activity and understands that the rocket is no longer the organization. He identifies a ridge relay as a lawful target and orders it seized while explicitly leaving municipal equipment untouched.
scenes.settingText: Tethergrid field interceptor on a high ridge — Cyrus with rangefinder, network trace highlighting one unauthorized relay box and municipal infrastructure clearly separated from it.

dialogueInline.speaker: Cyrus
dialogueInline.text: They’re not launching.

dialogueInline.speaker: Cyrus
dialogueInline.text: They’re connecting.

dialogueInline.speaker: Cyrus
dialogueInline.text: Seize the ridge node. Leave the municipal gear.

assetReuse.notes: Keep interceptor imagery; this replaces repeated binocular surveillance with a change in antagonist strategy.

scenes.summary: Cyrus’s team removes the ridge relay while Arvin, Lucia and Milo watch from the opposite canyon. Lucia starts to calculate a recovery route, but Milo shows that the remaining nodes already have a southern path. The crew chooses not to contest the seizure and tests the route-around instead.
scenes.settingText: Opposing canyon positions — Tethergrid team physically removing one compact relay, Launch-Shop crew observing from a safe ridge, alternate southern path marked on portable equipment.

dialogueInline.speaker: Cyrus
dialogueInline.text: This relay is unlicensed infrastructure.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: He practiced that.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: Do we need it?

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: No.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: Then let’s disappoint him.

assetReuse.notes: Use canyon standoff art; convert confrontation into proof that the system can afford to lose a node.

scenes.summary: With the ground lattice working around the seized node, Lucia plots the remaining geography and finds a ninety-three-kilometer basin gap beyond line-of-sight range. The crew finally identifies the one job orbit still has: a bridge between two independent ground clusters.
scenes.settingText: Launch-Shop exterior platform at dusk — Lucia’s tablet and paper basin map showing ground hops, one clear ninety-three-kilometer gap and two functioning clusters.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: Ground hops cover forty kilometers. The basin gap is ninety-three.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: So after all that, we still need a rocket.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: One.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: You sound offended.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: I was enjoying the quiet.

assetReuse.notes: Keep platform/map art; this is the first point where Issue 2 genuinely needs another launch.

scenes.summary: Lucia brings a military-grade interceptor shell stripped of seeker and warhead. Instead of turning the relay into a weapon, the crew uses the casing as a passive protective housing that makes the orbital bridge harder to seize or damage during deployment.
scenes.settingText: Launch-Shop loading platform — inert interceptor shell opened to show no seeker and no warhead, compact bridge relay fitting inside as passive protective casing.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: Interceptor shell. No warhead, no seeker.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: What does it do?

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: Makes the bridge harder to grab.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: Can we say ‘grab-resistant’ on the parts list?

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: Absolutely not.

assetReuse.notes: Salvage useful military-casing art while eliminating repetitive weaponization debate; Lucia already chooses the nonweapon use.

scenes.summary: The crew packs four locally signed ground keys and the compact bridge relay into the launch payload. No master credential exists in the vehicle; losing the rocket cannot grant authority over the ground network.
scenes.settingText: Launch-Shop payload-prep bay — compact bridge relay, four distinct locally signed keys, inert protective shell and rocket payload fairing ready for closure.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: Four ground keys, two routes, one bridge.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: And no master key.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: You say that like you’re checking for contraband.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: I am.

assetReuse.notes: Use loading/primer-crate composition without explosive primers; depict signed relay modules and payload hardware instead.

scenes.summary: The finished rocket rolls into position carrying a payload much smaller than the launch vehicle seems to deserve. Milo finishes the last continuity check while Arvin is pleased precisely because the orbital component is no longer the whole system.
scenes.settingText: Dry lakebed launch position at golden hour — finished Launch-Shop rocket, small sealed bridge payload, minimal crew and no excess weapon hardware.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: Payload’s almost insultingly small.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: Good.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: Don’t start.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: He loves saying that now.

assetReuse.notes: Keep strongest finished-rocket reveal, but make the small payload the point.

scenes.summary: The bridge rocket launches once while Tethergrid vehicles close on the lakebed. The dramatic question is not whether the crew can build a rocket again; it is whether the small bridge can join the already functioning ground clusters before the route closes.
scenes.settingText: Dry lakebed at dusk — single clean launch of the Copper Lattice bridge vehicle, Tethergrid vehicles distant enough to preserve safe corridor geography.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: Wind’s clean.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: Tethergrid?

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: Two minutes out.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: Plenty of time.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: That is not your line.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: I’m trying optimism.

assetReuse.notes: Use old launch page as Issue 2’s only true launch; rocket execution is compressed because Issue 1 already proved competence.

scenes.summary: As Tethergrid reaches the abandoned pad, the Launch-Shop crew is already moving with the portable timing modules while the bridge climbs overhead. They leave bulky launch tools behind because the ground clocks and local nodes are now more important than the vehicle.
scenes.settingText: Post-launch lakebed and departing Launch-Shop vehicle — vapor trail overhead, Tethergrid arriving at the pad, portable timing modules being carried while expendable launch tools remain.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: They’re on the pad.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: Bridge is already above them.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: Then leave the drills. Take the clocks.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: Never thought I’d hear that sentence.

assetReuse.notes: Keep vapor-trail/departure art; visually transfer importance from launch hardware to network hardware.

scenes.summary: The Copper Lattice activates across the basin. Esperanza hands a signed packet to the ridge network, the orbital bridge carries it across the ninety-three-kilometer gap, and Red Mesa accepts it under its own local clock. Coyote Wells receives status only, exactly as requested.
scenes.settingText: Multi-location Copper Lattice activation — Esperanza local node, ridge relay, small orbital bridge, Red Mesa controller and Coyote Wells read-only display connected by a clear comprehensible route.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: Esperanza to ridge. Ridge to bridge. Bridge to Red Mesa.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: Coyote Wells?

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: Read-only, like they asked.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: Again.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: You just want to watch it.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: Yes.

assetReuse.notes: NEW PAGE. This is the actual climax: several independent pieces work together for the first time.

scenes.summary: One ridge node disappears from the map after Tethergrid seizes it, but the packet path shifts south before anyone in Launch-Shop intervenes. Milo confirms the traffic arrived through the alternate route. For the first time the network survives a deliberate loss without asking Arvin what to do.
scenes.settingText: Launch-Shop network view paired with field image of a seized relay — one node dark, alternate southern path active, destination acknowledgment received without central override.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: Ridge node is gone.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: No—it’s just gone from the map.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: Difference?

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: Traffic moved south before I touched anything.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: There it is.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: There what is?

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: Repeatable.

assetReuse.notes: NEW PAGE. Pay off the issue thesis through behavior: route-around happens before the heroes can rescue the network.

scenes.summary: At sunrise the next morning, new requests begin stacking across three mismatched Launch-Shop displays faster than the crew can sort them. Some towns request purifier windows, others pump authorization or repair access, and even one town submits competing priorities. The Copper Lattice works; now access itself needs rules.
scenes.settingText: Launch-Shop control cabin at sunrise — three mismatched displays, rapidly multiplying community requests, paper strips and the stable Copper Lattice route still visible beneath the queue.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: Three new requests.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: Four.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: That one came twice.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: Same town, different priorities.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: So tomorrow we need rules.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: Before another rocket.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: Can tomorrow be after breakfast?

assetReuse.notes: NEW PAGE. Direct handoff into Public Sky: success creates a waiting list and a governance problem.

scenes.summary: At sunrise inside the Launch-Shop control cabin, Milo watches the request queue multiply across three mismatched displays while Arvin routes each request onto a physical paper strip and clips it to a board. The previous launch has widened the network faster than the crew expected: settlements want purifier windows, pump authorization and repair access, but the crew has only a few orbital windows to allocate.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: Seven communities before breakfast. We finally make this work and immediately discover success has a waiting list.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: Good problems can still kill people if you solve them carelessly.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: So what is the rule? First request, worst emergency, closest launch?

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: We do not have one yet. That is the problem we solve before we build another rocket.

scenes.summary: On the exterior work deck, Lucia lays three route transparencies over a sunlit basin map while Arvin and Milo secure a compact antenna frame beside her. Lucia shows that two aggressive launches could reach far more locked communities, but the schedule would leave almost no margin for verification, local draw limits or safe aborts.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: Every unused minute is somebody waiting on equipment that already works.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: And every bad authorization can empty a shared well that also already works.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: I am not arguing for careless. I am arguing that delay has a body count too.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: Then the queue needs to count both kinds of harm.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: Exactly. Reach is not the same thing as service.

scenes.summary: Milo converts the work deck into a crude allocation room using paper cards, grease-pencil columns and a portable basin display. With Arvin and Lucia testing edge cases, he separates requests by immediate health risk, remaining local reserve, shared-aquifer impact and whether the community has named people who can accept and enforce a draw limit. The board begins to look less like a mission list and more like public infrastructure.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: If we cannot explain why one town goes before another, we are not allocating. We are choosing favorites with better tools.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: Add retaliation risk. A town that accepts our help may pay for it after we leave.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: Add the right to refuse us entirely.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: You want the people asking for access to be able to tell us no?

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: Especially them.

scenes.summary: Long geometric rows of drought-resistant crops glow beneath efficient drip irrigation. A smiling agronomist checks a Tetherwell controller while animated statistics celebrate improved yield per allocated liter.
scenes.settingText: Tethergrid corporate-partnership film — immaculate agricultural infrastructure at golden hour.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tetherwell Narrator
dialogueInline.text: Tethergrid's high-efficiency agricultural partners produce more food with less water—protecting regional supply through another record drought.

scenes.summary: Inside the mobile workshop, Arvin bench-tests a community controller while Milo prints a one-page operating sheet and Lucia tries to break the procedure by asking what happens when a frightened operator skips a step. The protocol now requires visible limits, a local acknowledgement and a simple way for the community to replace Launch-Shop's settings with its own approved rules.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: If they need me to understand the machine, I have built another dependency.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: So the instructions have to survive us.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: And panic. Write them for the worst ten minutes of somebody's year.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: Good. No hidden controls, no proprietary repair lock, no permanent authority for us.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: You realize your revolution is becoming paperwork.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: That is how you know it intends to survive.

scenes.summary: Inside a Tethergrid mobile interception platform, Cyrus reviews the open request traffic and the new allocation rules on a glass display. He stops on a genuine Tetherwell suspension at Glass Basin, where a municipal purifier has less than a day of reserve, then overlays the community's location with a clean interception corridor. Rather than invent a false emergency, he orders his team to route the real need where Launch-Shop will see it.

dialogueInline.speaker: Cyrus
dialogueInline.text: Do not fabricate a crisis. Use the one the board already created.

dialogueInline.speaker: Cyrus
dialogueInline.text: If their rules are principles, urgency will not erase them.

dialogueInline.speaker: Cyrus
dialogueInline.text: If their rules are theater, Glass Basin will tell us before I have to.

scenes.summary: Back in the control cabin, a Glass Basin emergency packet rises to the top of Milo's new queue: 312 residents, purification reserve under eighteen hours, and a route that fits the next orbital window almost perfectly. Milo notices that the packet contains detailed equipment telemetry but no local approval key, while Lucia recognizes the corridor as unusually easy to fly.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: The need is real enough to verify. The route is what bothers me.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: It knows the pump, the reserve and the purifier load. It does not know who is allowed to say yes.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: Then we ask Glass Basin, not the packet.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: And if the window closes while we ask?

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: Then we lose a window. We do not borrow their consent because the clock is loud.

scenes.summary: Milo traces the Glass Basin packet across an old municipal relay, a public maintenance archive and Tetherwell service records while Arvin works the radio stack and Lucia compares route timing. They confirm that the purifier failure and access suspension are genuine, but the emergency wrapper entered the public network through a Tethergrid backbone node rather than from Glass Basin's local controller.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: The emergency is theirs. The invitation is not.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: Which means somebody wants us to help and somebody else wants to choose how we arrive.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: Good distinction.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: I would prefer distinctions that do not have interceptors attached.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: Those are less educational.

scenes.summary: The polished farm footage continues on one side while leaked pumping logs scroll on the other. Its uninterrupted premium allocation rises as three neighboring residential zones change from restricted to suspended.
scenes.settingText: The Dryline Report — split-screen analysis of leaked Tetherwell allocation records.

dialogueInline.speaker: Dryline Reporter
dialogueInline.text: The farm used more water during the emergency than all three locked communities combined. Its parent company sits on Tethergrid's board.

scenes.summary: Cyrus stands over a terrain model inside the interception platform while a technician places Glass Basin's actual municipal boundary beside the projected launch corridor. Cyrus orders the interceptor geometry moved farther from the settlement and forbids any kinetic action until the rocket clears the civilian footprint, even though the safer interception point gives Launch-Shop more time.

dialogueInline.speaker: Cyrus
dialogueInline.text: Move the intercept south.

dialogueInline.speaker: Cyrus
dialogueInline.text: The board asked for the satellite. It did not authorize me to turn a water emergency into a crater.

dialogueInline.speaker: Cyrus
dialogueInline.text: Let them reach the hard part of their own argument. I want to know whether they still believe it when belief costs them something.

scenes.summary: At the workshop bench, Milo builds the Glass Basin authorization package as a physical stack of modules: queue rank, maximum draw, local quorum, public audit log and an emergency rollback that returns the purifier to a safe state if the satellite disappears. Arvin deliberately lets Milo make the final architecture choices while Lucia attacks each module from the perspective of an adversary.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: Two local keys can start the window. Three can raise the draw cap. Any one can stop it.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: And if one key is stolen?

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: The other two see the change in the public log before it takes effect.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: Your design. Your go or no-go.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: You are giving me the abort?

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: I am recognizing that you already built it.

scenes.summary: On a limestone ridge above the launch site, Lucia lays out a decoy route that keeps the real ascent away from Glass Basin and gives Tethergrid less reason to fire near civilians. The safer geometry reaches fewer communities than her earlier plan, and she marks those lost opportunities on the map instead of pretending they do not matter.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: This route protects Glass Basin and costs us two other windows.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: Yesterday you would have hated that sentence.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: I hate it today.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: And?

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: And reach is not service if the people underneath it did not choose the risk. Write that into the rule.

scenes.summary: Minutes before the first launch window, the crew sends Glass Basin a plain-language disclosure showing the suspected Tethergrid trap, the proposed draw cap, the retaliation risk and a choice to accept, defer or request another route. The reply channel goes dead under deliberate interference. Milo watches the countdown pass the point where they could still launch on an inferred yes, and nobody reaches for the ignition controls.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: We know they need it. We know what they would probably say.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: Probably is what power says when it is tired of asking.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: Let the window go.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: That is twelve hours we cannot give back.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: Correct. And it is still their twelve hours to risk, not ours.

scenes.summary: After dark, a signed Glass Basin packet arrives through an independent Dryline relay assembled from three local maintenance keys. The community accepts the exposure, chooses a six-hour purifier window below the shared draw limit and explicitly rejects any wider pump authorization. Milo verifies each key while Arvin and Lucia read the same terms over his shoulders.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: Three signatures. Six hours. Purifier only. No agricultural draw.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: They chose less access than we could give them.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: Which is why it is access instead of rescue.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: You have been waiting all day to say that.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: I had twelve hours to edit.

scenes.summary: At the field launch site, Milo runs the checklist from the center position while Arvin works feed pressure and Lucia manages the route and decoy timing. The arrangement is visibly different from earlier launches: Milo calls each hold point, Arvin answers to him on the propulsion system, and Lucia waits for his clearance before committing the route.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: Pressure stable. Community keys valid. Draw cap loaded. Arv, you are green.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: That sounded distressingly authoritative.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: You gave me the abort.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: I know. I am enjoying the consequences.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: Enjoy faster. Route opens in forty seconds.

scenes.summary: Inside the Tethergrid interception platform, Cyrus sees the signed community keys appear in the launch telemetry just as a board directive authorizes seizure of the satellite. He studies the quorum, the published cap and the local rollback, then moves the intercept point one final time so any debris will fall away from Glass Basin.

dialogueInline.speaker: Cyrus
dialogueInline.text: They put the users inside the control loop.

dialogueInline.speaker: Cyrus
dialogueInline.text: That is either naïve or inconveniently serious.

dialogueInline.speaker: Cyrus
dialogueInline.text: Intercept after civilian clear. I want the satellite, not an argument written in casualties.

scenes.summary: The rocket clears the ridge and the short-lived satellite opens the Glass Basin corridor. Tethergrid closes on the spacecraft faster than expected, leaving Lucia one burst of bandwidth before interception. The console offers two choices: open additional nearby equipment that never opted in, or spend the burst warning every enrolled community that this route is compromised while delivering Glass Basin's six-hour local authorization and shutdown instructions. Lucia selects the warning.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: One burst. We can open three more zones or push the warning and Glass Basin's local token.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: Lucia, your route.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: Then it carries what people agreed to.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: Warning selected.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: Send it. Nobody becomes collateral to our success.

scenes.summary: Tethergrid disables the satellite over empty desert, but Glass Basin's controller has already cached the six-hour authorization and every enrolled community receives the compromised-route warning. In the Launch-Shop cabin, Milo watches the orbital icon vanish while the Glass Basin purifier remains green under its locally enforced cap. Arvin quietly marks the lost satellite off the board instead of treating the mission as a failure.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: Satellite is gone.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: Glass Basin?

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: Purifier is still running. Six-hour token is local. Draw cap is holding.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: Then the machine knew when to stop needing us.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: That may be the first thing we built today that feels bigger than a launch.

scenes.summary: At dawn, the request board fills again, but the new packets are different: communities attach their own draw rules, quorum lists and shutdown conditions instead of merely asking Launch-Shop to decide for them. Milo pins the first contested override request at the edge of the board, where one local operator wants a higher emergency draw cap and the neighboring quorum is still incomplete. Arvin leaves it visibly pending.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: First override request. Heat emergency. They want to raise the cap before the neighboring keys agree.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: Public ownership lasted almost one night before somebody argued with it.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: Good.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: Good?

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: A system nobody is allowed to argue with is just Tetherwell with friendlier people. We answer when everyone affected can see the question.

scenes.summary: At a damaged community wellhead, Tamsin walks Arvin, Milo and Lucia through a cracked pump casing and the controller history from the first serious Public Sky failure. The pump exceeded its safe draw window only after a local user removed the shared limiter. Tamsin makes clear that she approved the access window, not the override.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tamsin
dialogueInline.text: We asked for six hours. The stop came off without us.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: Three taps. That's all the bypass took. I made the bad choice the easy one.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: Then I own part of the failure.

scenes.summary: Milo rebuilds the event from cached controller logs while Arvin measures the damaged pump. The shared limit itself was correct; the design failed because a single local credential could defeat it without a second person seeing the change. Lucia pushes them to separate accountability from blame before the whole network panics.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: Skip the shame for now. What do we make impossible?

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: One person could make a basin decision from a maintenance screen.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: Not again. If one screen can change everybody's water, one screen has too much authority.

scenes.summary: Inside a Tethergrid command platform, Cyrus reviews the same pump failure alongside basin-pressure data. He refuses a staff recommendation to describe the pump as destroyed by an unknown pirate command; the cause is already clear enough. He authorizes publication of the real failure because the truth is damaging on its own.

dialogueInline.speaker: Cyrus
dialogueInline.text: Use the casing. Use the draw curve. Leave the adjectives out.

dialogueInline.speaker: Cyrus
dialogueInline.text: Do not hand them a propaganda complaint when the pump already makes our case.

scenes.summary: A technician examines a cracked pump casing beside a community controller running the Launch-Shop's open protocol. A draw-history graph shows the pump exceeding its safe window after a local operator removed the shared limit.
scenes.settingText: The Dryline Report — forensic field report at a damaged community wellhead.

dialogueInline.speaker: Dryline Reporter
dialogueInline.text: Open access did not create more water. Someone overrode the community limit, damaged this pump and shortened the neighboring wells' remaining season.

scenes.summary: Back at the wellhead, Lucia tells Arvin they must publish their own logs before Tethergrid frames the incident for them. Arvin worries that halting the affected node will leave families short of water tonight. Tamsin rejects the false choice: tell the community exactly what happened, show the remaining safe volume, and let them decide how to use it.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: If we suspend this node, people lose water tonight.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tamsin
dialogueInline.text: Give me the safe number. Give me what happens past it. Then let us decide.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: Fine. Put the choice on the board.

scenes.summary: In the mobile workshop, Milo turns the failure into hardware: a physical trip module, a tamper-evident maintenance key and a two-person confirmation for any change that affects another well. Arvin helps simplify the mechanism until a tired operator can understand its state without a manual.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: Red means the pump stops. Amber means ask another human being. No hidden menu.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: And no master password in my pocket.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: You're really giving that up?

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: Should have done it sooner.

scenes.summary: Cyrus approves a basin-wide Tetherwell advisory using photographs of the damaged pump and a technically accurate explanation of what an overridden draw limit can do to neighboring wells. He removes a marketing line that calls every Public Sky node unsafe, then lets the harder evidence stand.

dialogueInline.speaker: Cyrus
dialogueInline.text: Show the cracked casing. Show the draw curve. Remove the adjective.

dialogueInline.speaker: Cyrus
dialogueInline.text: People can be frightened by facts without our help.

scenes.summary: The cracked community pump is isolated against severe black graphics. Red unauthorized-signal rings spread from it across a basin map before the Tetherwell shield closes around unaffected users.
scenes.settingText: Tetherwell emergency advisory — authoritative graphics and selectively edited field footage.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tetherwell Narrator
dialogueInline.text: The Launch-Shop calls it liberation. Water systems call it damage. Only verified Tetherwell control can protect the whole basin.

scenes.summary: Representatives from several communities crowd around basin maps in a municipal room while Tamsin moderates an angry meeting. Some want Launch-Shop to restore unrestricted access before Tethergrid uses the failure as an excuse to shut them all down. Milo lays the damaged limiter on the table and explains exactly where their first design gave too much power to one person.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: This part did what we told it to do. That is the problem.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tamsin
dialogueInline.text: The aquifer doesn't care how we vote. The allocation still does.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: And nobody gets to change everybody else's number alone.

scenes.summary: At three neighboring wellheads, Milo and Tamsin run the first live test of the new trip modules. Physical lamps show each well's draw, reserve and lock state in plain view. When one pump approaches the shared threshold, all three sites see the same warning before the trip engages.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tamsin
dialogueInline.text: I can explain this to somebody who has never met you.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: That may be the nicest thing anyone has said about my wiring.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: It is the requirement now.

scenes.summary: Arvin and Lucia argue beside the test rack about where authority should stop. Arvin wants a hard emergency floor that no remote user can defeat. Lucia insists communities must still choose priorities above that floor. They settle on a narrow invariant: no command may push a shared source past its measured physical limit; everything else belongs to the people sharing it.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: If your safeguard can overrule everybody, you rebuilt Tetherwell.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: If it can't stop a pump, it's a sticker.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: Stop the pump. Don't pick the winner.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: That I can build.

scenes.summary: Cyrus watches Public Sky traffic settle after the new trip modules go live. The failure rate falls instead of rising. He recognizes that Launch-Shop has responded to a public mistake by surrendering unilateral control, which makes the network harder to dismiss as reckless improvisation.

dialogueInline.speaker: Cyrus
dialogueInline.text: They published it.

dialogueInline.speaker: Cyrus
dialogueInline.text: That makes the next failure harder to use against them.

scenes.summary: A neighboring settlement requests more water than its fair share after a refrigeration breakdown threatens a medicine store. Tamsin's own community can cover part of the difference only by giving up irrigation for the night. She puts the choice to both groups, and the transfer is approved openly rather than granted by Launch-Shop.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tamsin
dialogueInline.text: We can give you twelve thousand liters. It costs us tomorrow's irrigation.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: You do not need our permission.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tamsin
dialogueInline.text: Good. We were not asking for it.

scenes.summary: At a field launch site, the crew prepares a compact relay whose only job is to synchronize the new shared-limit tables before Tethergrid closes the pass. Milo catches a temperature sensor drifting just before fueling and replaces it rather than accepting a bad reading to save time.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: We can launch on schedule or launch with a temperature we actually know.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: We know which one counts.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: I will buy you six minutes. Use five.

scenes.summary: The relay clears the pad, but Tethergrid begins jamming the uplink before the full table can propagate. Across the basin, local controllers fall back to cached limits and continue operating without asking Launch-Shop for instructions. The partial outage becomes the first real test of whether Public Sky can function without constant central supervision.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: We lost half the uplink.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: And the wells?

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: Still inside their local limits.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: Then stop staring at what we lost.

scenes.summary: One isolated pump begins cavitating as its local reservoir empties faster than forecast. Arvin has a maintenance command that could force another minute of draw, but using it would violate the new rule they just published. He calls Tamsin instead. She orders the pump shut down and reroutes the remaining water by truck.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: I can force sixty more seconds.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tamsin
dialogueInline.text: Will it hurt the shared source?

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: It might.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tamsin
dialogueInline.text: Then shut it down. We will move the water we already have.

scenes.summary: Cyrus receives confirmation that Launch-Shop allowed a Public Sky node to go dark rather than defeat its own safeguard. The choice denies him the easy argument that they will always choose access over conservation. He orders his analysts to stop modeling Arvin as the network's sole decision-maker.

dialogueInline.speaker: Cyrus
dialogueInline.text: They had the override.

dialogueInline.speaker: Cyrus
dialogueInline.text: They didn't use it.

dialogueInline.speaker: Cyrus
dialogueInline.text: Rebuild the model. We're tracking a network now.

scenes.summary: At sunset, communities pin their next-day draw allocations to public boards beside the controllers. Tamsin notices that even with every participating well inside its new limit, the regional groundwater trend is falling faster than Tethergrid's public forecast. Milo copies the discrepancy for Arvin. The network has solved one governance problem and exposed a larger shortage.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tamsin
dialogueInline.text: The limits add up. The water still does not.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: Then somebody's forecast is missing a very large number.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: Find the number before we decide what it means.

scenes.summary: In the Launch-Shop control cabin, Milo overlays Public Sky draw logs against groundwater telemetry from participating communities. Every node is staying inside the new limits, yet the basin is dropping much faster than Tethergrid's public drought model predicts. Arvin makes him check the boring explanations first: sensor drift, delayed recharge and duplicate measurements.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: If our numbers are wrong, they are wrong in twelve places the same way.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: Good. Now prove the impossible thing after the ordinary things fail.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: And before we accuse anyone who owns lawyers.

scenes.summary: Tamsin brings handwritten reservoir and well ledgers from communities that were never connected to Public Sky. Their physical measurements match Milo's decline. The discrepancy predates the expanded network, which means the missing draw is elsewhere.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tamsin
dialogueInline.text: These books never touched your network. Same drop.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: So we did not cause the missing water.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: That is not the same as knowing who did.

scenes.summary: Lucia cross-references publicly filed agricultural allocations, tanker permits and Tethergrid emergency notices. Several premium users continue drawing at levels that cannot fit inside the public model. She hands Arvin a list of discrepancies, not an accusation, and asks what evidence would make the conclusion defensible.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: I have a pattern. Tell me what would turn it into evidence.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: Independent telemetry and a physical draw we can observe.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: For once the difficult part is not the rocket.

scenes.summary: Before they have complete proof, Arvin calls for Public Sky communities to reduce discretionary draw by ten percent because the physical water level is real regardless of who caused the shortage. Tamsin agrees to put the reduction to the communities rather than present it as an order from Launch-Shop.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: I cannot prove where the missing water went. I can prove the basin is lower than we planned.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tamsin
dialogueInline.text: Then that's what goes on the board: low basin, unknown cause.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: Harder to punch holes in.

scenes.summary: Reservoir gauges fall through orange warning bands as a basin map develops expanding pressure gaps. Unauthorized satellite icons are overlaid on the decline while a formal Tethergrid seal replaces the ordinary Tetherwell branding.
scenes.settingText: Tethergrid drought-response announcement — severe corporate broadcast distributed basin-wide.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tetherwell Narrator
dialogueInline.text: Unauthorized network interference is destabilizing coordinated supply during a critical shortage. Emergency restrictions begin at midnight.

scenes.summary: After Tethergrid blames unauthorized network interference for the worsening shortage, angry community delegates demand that Launch-Shop increase their allocations before new restrictions arrive. Milo refuses to turn the public ledger into a race for the last water and demonstrates a reserve-margin column that leaves part of every shared source deliberately unused.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: This column is water we can reach and still choose not to take.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tamsin
dialogueInline.text: People are going to hate that column.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: I already hate it. That is why it is probably honest.

scenes.summary: Inside Tethergrid, Cyrus reviews an internal basin forecast dated weeks before the first Public Sky expansion. It predicted the current emergency. A board directive beside it protects premium industrial and agricultural contracts from the first round of restrictions. Cyrus understands that the conservation problem is real and the allocation order is indefensible.

dialogueInline.speaker: Cyrus
dialogueInline.text: This forecast predates their first relay.

dialogueInline.speaker: Cyrus
dialogueInline.text: So the drop was already underway.

scenes.summary: Lucia and Tamsin help Dryline verify a leaked copy of the same reservoir telemetry against independent physical measurements. They refuse to publish a dramatic claim until the timestamps, sensor calibration and premium draw records reconcile. The evidence survives the check.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: If one timestamp is wrong, they will use it to bury everything else.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tamsin
dialogueInline.text: Then check it twice. People can wait an hour for a story they can trust.

scenes.summary: Raw reservoir telemetry appears beneath Tethergrid's public graph. The decline begins weeks before the first unauthorized satellite, while concealed premium draw contracts continue as residential restrictions deepen.
scenes.settingText: The Dryline Report — leaked telemetry reconstructed on a portable newsroom display.

dialogueInline.speaker: Dryline Reporter
dialogueInline.text: Tethergrid knew the basin was failing twenty-three days ago. It protected premium contracts, concealed the projections and blamed the network that exposed the shortage.

scenes.summary: Community delegates use Milo's reserve-margin board to make their first basin-wide emergency allocations. Drinking water, clinic cooling, livestock, food production and household use compete openly on the same page. No option is painless. Arvin stays out of the chair while Tamsin forces the group to name what each choice costs.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tamsin
dialogueInline.text: If your line gets more, point to the line that gets less.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: That's the whole equation.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: Put it on the board.

scenes.summary: At a reservoir service road, Lucia and Milo watch a permitted Tethergrid tanker convoy draw from an industrial loading point while a nearby municipal line remains physically valved shut. They document the hardware state and leave without interfering with the active supply equipment.
scenes.settingText: Mojave reservoir service road — blue water held between pale ridges, municipal pipework, industrial loading hardware and severe high-desert light.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: The municipal pipe is not dry. It is closed.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: Photograph the valve tag, the meter and the tanker manifest. Touch nothing.

scenes.summary: Tethergrid offers selected communities restored priority access if they disconnect from Public Sky and return to exclusive Tetherwell control. The offer is materially useful, not empty propaganda. Tamsin refuses to answer for anyone else and schedules separate votes at every affected community.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tamsin
dialogueInline.text: Some places may take the deal. That's their call.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: Then nobody on our side punishes them for saying yes.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: If leaving costs you water, it isn't voluntary.

scenes.summary: The votes split. Several communities return to Tetherwell because they need immediate certainty; others remain on Public Sky and accept lower shared limits. Milo removes the departing nodes cleanly from the allocation table instead of treating the loss as sabotage. The remaining network becomes smaller and more credible.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: Three left. Two stayed. Nobody broke anything.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: Then the system worked.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: That is a brutal definition of working.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: It is a voluntary one.

scenes.summary: With Tethergrid preparing to close the remaining orbital corridor, the crew assembles one last compact relay. Arvin strips optional throughput hardware from the payload so its remaining capacity is dedicated to safety tables, reserve margins and community coordination rather than increased draw.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: We are launching less capability on purpose.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: Less extraction. More coordination.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: The least glamorous satellite we have ever loved.

scenes.summary: Cyrus authorizes reuse of Tetherwell's original conservation film while the board prepares emergency restrictions. Watching the serene reservoir footage, he notices how carefully the old film talks about preserving water without ever explaining who gets access to the preserved reserve.

dialogueInline.speaker: Cyrus
dialogueInline.text: Use the old film.

dialogueInline.speaker: Cyrus
dialogueInline.text: Don't change a frame. The omission does the work.

scenes.summary: A vast blue reservoir reflects the sunrise between pale desert ridges. The camera glides across the calm surface toward an immaculate control tower as the old Tetherwell emblem appears.
scenes.settingText: Tetherwell legacy film — serene reservoir photography from the original conservation campaign.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tetherwell Narrator
dialogueInline.text: Coordinated conservation preserved this water through the longest drought in recorded history. Tetherwell keeps the future in reserve.

scenes.summary: The same reservoir shot widens beyond the corporate crop. A convoy of Tethergrid tankers draws from an industrial loading point while the dry municipal pipeline to a nearby settlement remains physically valved shut.
scenes.settingText: The Dryline Report — the uncropped source footage behind a Tetherwell legacy film.

dialogueInline.speaker: Dryline Reporter
dialogueInline.text: The reservoir was never empty. Access was. The water is scarce; the truth does not have to be.

scenes.summary: After Dryline publishes the uncropped reservoir evidence, Public Sky communities begin posting Tethergrid premium allocations beside their own reduced draw schedules. The contrast turns the fight from a secret technical dispute into a visible argument about legitimate scarcity and illegitimate priority.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tamsin
dialogueInline.text: We are taking less because the basin is low.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: And they are taking more because their contract says they can.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: Put both numbers on the same board.

scenes.summary: Lucia wants to release every leaked Tethergrid document at once. Arvin insists that Dryline separate verified records from material they cannot authenticate. Tamsin sides with him, arguing that trust is now infrastructure too.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: There's enough here without the weak pages.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tamsin
dialogueInline.text: Good. Then cut anything we can't prove.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: We don't need it.

scenes.summary: Cyrus invokes emergency orbital authority to close the corridor used by Launch-Shop's short-lived relays. He frames the action as protection of shared infrastructure during a drought, and the authority is real. He also knows it will protect Tetherwell's commercial moat.

dialogueInline.speaker: Cyrus
dialogueInline.text: Close the unlicensed corridor at midnight.

dialogueInline.speaker: Cyrus
dialogueInline.text: Use emergency-load authority.

dialogueInline.speaker: Cyrus
dialogueInline.text: It is defensible. That's enough.

scenes.summary: The final relay launches minutes before the corridor closes and carries the new reserve tables across the basin. Its service window is brief. As the last uplink drops away, Arvin looks at the ground equipment rather than the sky and tells the crew the next version cannot depend on orbit for ordinary coordination.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: That was the last clean pass.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: For now.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: Then orbit stops being the whole network.

scenes.summary: Days after the orbital corridor closes, Public Sky communities continue operating from cached local limits, but neighboring basins can no longer reconcile changes quickly enough to share emergencies. Tamsin arrives with three paper ledgers that disagree by hours rather than liters. The system is surviving, but it is becoming blind at the edges.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tamsin
dialogueInline.text: Nothing is collapsing. That is the good news.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: The bad news is we now reconcile a regional water network with pencils.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: Pencils are allowed. Delay is the problem.

scenes.summary: Milo demonstrates a ground-relay prototype that can pass allocation changes from ridge to ridge without orbital support. A voltage surge from a pump starter welds its delicate electronic pressure switch closed. Arvin recognizes that the relay needs a mechanical trip device built for brutal industrial transients, not laboratory electronics.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: It survived the desert, the dust and me. Then a pump starter killed it in one blink.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: Good failure. It told us what the environment actually is.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: Do you know where to find something less polite?

scenes.summary: Tamsin maps communities that can relay updates by line of sight, existing utility conduit and scheduled vehicle routes. Her plan keeps local control intact while creating several independent paths between basins. Arvin realizes the communications problem is as much organizational as technical.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tamsin
dialogueInline.text: We already move medicine, parts and people between these places every day.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: Then the network has routes I never designed.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tamsin
dialogueInline.text: Exactly.

scenes.summary: Cyrus deploys lawful interference against the remaining unlicensed radio bands but orders his teams not to disable well telemetry that Tetherwell itself needs for basin safety. The constraint leaves narrow physical and procedural paths the distributed network can use.

dialogueInline.speaker: Cyrus
dialogueInline.text: Jam the unauthorized carriers. Leave Tetherwell telemetry alone.

dialogueInline.speaker: Cyrus
dialogueInline.text: I said carriers. Not wells.

scenes.summary: Arvin identifies a decommissioned hydroelectric service gallery whose old mechanical governor used a pressure switch designed to survive decades of surges, damp air and vibration. Lucia plans a retrieval route that avoids the active flood-control side of the dam and treats the structure as infrastructure, not a treasure chest.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: We take nothing connected to live flood control.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: That removes most of the interesting hardware.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: It also removes drowning a town from the failure modes.

scenes.summary: Inside the decommissioned gallery, Arvin and Lucia cross a wet service ledge to reach the old governor cabinet. Lucia slips on moss at the spillway edge; Arvin catches her wrist against the railing while Milo secures a safety line. The physical danger comes from the structure, not betrayal within the crew.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: I have you. Milo, line first.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: I am stable.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: You can be stable and clipped in at the same time.

scenes.summary: The pressure switch they came for is still part of a dormant-but-required emergency gate circuit. Removing it would leave the spillway without a mechanical backup if the modern controller fails. Instead of taking it, Milo measures the spring geometry, contact travel and diaphragm area while Arvin photographs every mechanical interface.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: We found the perfect part and are leaving it here.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: Because it already has a job.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: Take the measurements. Respect is cheaper than a flood.

scenes.summary: Back at the Launch-Shop, Milo fabricates a rugged duplicate from a spare turbine governor, a ceramic contact block and a machined spring seat. The device has no software path around its emergency trip. Tamsin asks for one feature Arvin did not consider: an obvious manual indicator so a local operator can tell why it opened.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tamsin
dialogueInline.text: If it trips at two in the morning, I need to know whether to call a mechanic or wake the whole basin.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: Mechanical flag. Big enough to read while angry.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: Excellent specification.

scenes.summary: Cyrus reviews Tethergrid's public case against offline coordination. The legitimate risk is that disconnected wells can make locally safe choices that become unsafe in aggregate. He approves a documentary warning about that failure mode but refuses language claiming that only Tethergrid can coordinate shared water in principle.

dialogueInline.speaker: Cyrus
dialogueInline.text: Use 'isolation risk.' Drop the rest. Legal will know why.

scenes.summary: A precise basin diagram separates into disconnected local clusters. Individually safe pump icons turn amber when their combined draw arrives too late for the central model to reconcile.
scenes.settingText: Tetherwell network-safety film — clean basin map showing isolated wells and delayed coordination.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tetherwell Narrator
dialogueInline.text: Water can be overdrawn by individually reasonable decisions. Shared resources require shared timing, not merely good intentions.

scenes.summary: Tamsin and Milo define the ground-loop rule: any change that affects another community must travel by at least two independent paths before it becomes basin-wide, while an isolated site automatically tightens its local reserve. The result is slower than Tetherwell and far harder to decapitate.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: Fast path plus witness path.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tamsin
dialogueInline.text: And if both disappear?

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: The local limit gets stricter, not looser.

scenes.summary: Three communities test the rule through ridge relays and a scheduled maintenance truck carrying a sealed update card. One electronic path fails. The physical courier closes the loop later, and the system reconciles without anyone receiving an invisible emergency override from Launch-Shop.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tamsin
dialogueInline.text: It took forty-one minutes.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: And nobody had to trust a person they could not see.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: I am learning to enjoy slow success.

scenes.summary: Paper ledgers, physical trip flags and ridge-relay status lamps are compared across three communities. One delayed update is visibly marked and corrected before the next draw period begins.
scenes.settingText: The Dryline Report — community coordination desks and ridge relays operating during the orbital closure.

dialogueInline.speaker: Dryline Reporter
dialogueInline.text: The new network is slower without orbit. It is also still rationing. During this outage, participating wells reduced combined draw instead of increasing it.

scenes.summary: The crew installs the first permanent ground relay on a limestone ridge. Tethergrid interference sweeps across the ordinary radio bands, forcing the node onto its slower alternate path. The mechanical trip remains stable through repeated pump-start surges.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: Carrier is gone. Alternate path is alive.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: Pressure trip?

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: Still exactly where we left it.

scenes.summary: Cyrus traces the new relay to a ridge that also carries Tetherwell telemetry for the same basin. A broad shutdown would make enforcement easier and water management worse. He orders a targeted seizure team instead, accepting that physical due process is slower than remote control.

dialogueInline.speaker: Cyrus
dialogueInline.text: Do not turn off the ridge.

dialogueInline.speaker: Cyrus
dialogueInline.text: If we want the box, send people to the box.

scenes.summary: Lucia leads the Launch-Shop vehicles along a visible decoy route while Tamsin's community crews quietly move the relay's duplicate components to two other ridges. The tactic protects redundancy rather than attacking Tethergrid personnel or equipment.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: Let them follow the vehicle that looks important.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tamsin
dialogueInline.text: The ugly boxes are already moving.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: I worked very hard to make those ugly boxes.

scenes.summary: Arvin removes the Launch-Shop master override from the ground-loop controller and divides recovery authority among community-held physical keys. Tamsin tests that Arvin himself cannot raise a shared limit without the same local confirmations required of everyone else.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: Try my credential.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tamsin
dialogueInline.text: Denied.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: You look pleased to be powerless.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: In this specific way, yes.

scenes.summary: Tethergrid seizes one relay cabinet. The neighboring nodes route around it using the duplicate mechanical trips, utility conduit and scheduled physical updates. Cyrus watches the basin remain coordinated after removing a component he expected to matter.

dialogueInline.speaker: Cyrus
dialogueInline.text: Cabinet's gone.

dialogueInline.speaker: Cyrus
dialogueInline.text: Traffic isn't.

scenes.summary: At dawn, the ground loop is slow, inelegant and functioning. Tamsin points out that separated regions beyond the ridge chain still need periodic orbital bridges. Milo rolls out a heat-scarred nose-cone mockup: the next relay must climb faster and survive a much harsher intercept environment.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tamsin
dialogueInline.text: We made it three days without orbit.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: Next basin won't.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: Then we build something that can take the trip.

scenes.summary: Tethergrid emergency licensing blocks ordinary purchase of aerospace-grade heat-shield tiles and high-temperature adhesive anywhere near the Launch-Shop's operating region. Milo demonstrates why they need both: the new relay trajectory has a steeper, faster climb and the test nose cone chars through an unprotected panel in seconds.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: The old skin survives the old flight. This is not the old flight.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: Then design around what we can actually buy.

scenes.summary: Arvin identifies refractory ceramic from a decommissioned industrial furnace as a workable tile source. The available bonding compound is hazardous but manageable with ventilation, proper respirators and strict cure timing. Lucia rejects an easier recovery route through an active chemical store because stealing from a live facility would shift their risk onto workers who never chose it.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: Decommissioned furnace. Documented waste stream. No live process. Fine.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: You make responsible theft sound very bureaucratic.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: Salvage. And yes.

scenes.summary: Tamsin coordinates community workshops that can cut and gauge simple shield tiles to Milo's published dimensions. Her public explanations make the process reproducible outside Launch-Shop, and her name becomes associated with the network instead of remaining safely invisible.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tamsin
dialogueInline.text: Doesn't pass the gauge, it goes in the reject bin. I don't care whose initials are on it.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: You have become alarmingly good at quality control.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tamsin
dialogueInline.text: You taught us to return bad parts.

scenes.summary: Cyrus tells his enforcement team to stop treating Launch-Shop hardware as the only target. The network now survives equipment seizures because communities reproduce parts and rules. He directs investigators toward public coordinators and documented logistics while prohibiting speculative raids on uninvolved settlements.

dialogueInline.speaker: Cyrus
dialogueInline.text: Stop counting rockets. Count workshops, freight and approvals.

dialogueInline.speaker: Cyrus
dialogueInline.text: Bring me evidence, not a map full of guesses.

scenes.summary: Lucia tells Tamsin that her increasingly public role has made her identifiable to Tethergrid. She recommends stepping back until the launch is complete. Tamsin refuses to disappear entirely but agrees to publish only work she is willing to defend publicly and to move sensitive coordination to rotating community delegates.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: You are visible now. I need you to understand what that changes.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tamsin
dialogueInline.text: I know. I'm not going to be stupid. I'm also not disappearing because they noticed me.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: Then we reduce the part only you can do.

scenes.summary: At the decommissioned furnace complex, the crew recovers intact refractory panels and sealed drums of approved high-temperature compound from a documented disposal lot. They work in respirators and portable ventilation while Milo tracks exposure time and container condition instead of treating the chemical hazard as atmosphere.
scenes.settingText: Decommissioned industrial furnace complex — intact refractory structures, ventilated work zones, tagged hazardous-material areas, maintained salvage equipment and bright desert light outside.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: Drum seal is good. Ventilation is good. Timer starts when we open it.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: And if any one of those stops being true?

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: We leave.

scenes.summary: The first full-scale burn test fails. A long strip of bonded tile begins to peel as the nose cone heats, and Arvin aborts before the test article destroys itself. Milo is frustrated until he sees that the intact segments failed at their joints rather than through the ceramic. The controlled loss gives them the answer without costing the vehicle.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: We had twelve more seconds.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: And no reason to spend them.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: The ceramic lived. The seam moved.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: That is the useful part of the failure.

scenes.summary: Tethergrid prepares a public safety piece showing the failed burn test and warning about amateur high-energy flight. Cyrus allows the footage because the hazard is real, but orders the edit to include the crew's visible abort rather than imply an uncontrolled explosion.

dialogueInline.speaker: Cyrus
dialogueInline.text: Keep the abort in.

dialogueInline.speaker: Cyrus
dialogueInline.text: Cut it and Dryline puts it back by lunch.

scenes.summary: A test nose cone glows under heat as a strip of ceramic begins to peel. The frame freezes on the lifted edge while an abort marker appears beside the temperature curve.
scenes.settingText: Tethergrid launch-safety advisory — controlled footage of the failed ablative burn test.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tetherwell Narrator
dialogueInline.text: High-energy flight punishes small material errors at extraordinary speed. Unlicensed test programs transfer that risk to everyone beneath the corridor.

scenes.summary: Dryline compares the failed test with Launch-Shop's published temperature, bond and abort data. The report notes that the failure was real and that the complete test record was released voluntarily, while Tethergrid does not publish equivalent data from its own interception systems.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tamsin
dialogueInline.text: Leave the ugly graph in.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: I was not going to hide it.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tamsin
dialogueInline.text: I know. That is why people are still listening.

scenes.summary: The same failure footage continues beside the full temperature trace, bond data and visible abort threshold. A second panel lists the interception-test data Tethergrid does not publish.
scenes.settingText: The Dryline Report — side-by-side review of the failed burn and the complete published test record.

dialogueInline.speaker: Dryline Reporter
dialogueInline.text: The failure is real. So is the abort. Launch-Shop published the complete test record within an hour. Tethergrid does not release comparable interception data.

scenes.summary: Milo redesigns the heat shield as small independently retained tiles with narrow expansion gaps and copper edge clips that community workshops can reproduce. The solution pays off the crew's earlier doctrine: a repeatable small part is more valuable than one perfect hand-built surface.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: No heroic sheet of ceramic. Two hundred boring tiles.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: Boring scales.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: Put that on the workshop wall and never say it again.

scenes.summary: The second burn test holds through the full profile. Several tiles char sacrificially, exactly as designed, while the structure beneath remains cool enough to fly. Community-made replacements from three workshops all pass the same gauge afterward.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: Surface is ruined.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: Structure is intact.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tamsin
dialogueInline.text: So ruined was the job.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: I like her version better.

scenes.summary: Tethergrid correlates Tamsin's public burn-test update with travel records and identifies the community coordination site she is using. Cyrus signs a narrow detention order based on documented interference with Tetherwell operations and tells the arrest team that the objective is custody, not intimidation of the settlement.

dialogueInline.speaker: Cyrus
dialogueInline.text: One warrant. One person. Don't turn a pickup into a sweep.

dialogueInline.speaker: Cyrus
dialogueInline.text: If it's not in the order, don't touch it.

scenes.summary: Lucia learns that Tethergrid units are moving toward Tamsin's location and calls her with enough time to leave. Tamsin chooses instead to finish distributing the new shield verification tables and rotate her remaining network authority to other community delegates before she moves.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: You have minutes, not hours.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tamsin
dialogueInline.text: Then I need three of them.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: For what?

dialogueInline.speaker: Tamsin
dialogueInline.text: To make sure taking me does not take anything else.

scenes.summary: Tamsin completes the authority transfer, closes the coordinator console and walks out before Tethergrid enters the building. She does not force her neighbors into a confrontation on her behalf. Cyrus's team detains her without a firefight, but the copied keys and procedures are already elsewhere.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tamsin
dialogueInline.text: Board's closed. Pump authority is transferred.

scenes.summary: Lucia reaches the ridge above the settlement too late to prevent the detention convoy from leaving. She could attack the transport route, but doing so would turn Tamsin's neighbors into a battlefield. She marks the convoy route and returns to the crew with a rescue problem instead of an impulsive retaliation.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: I can stop it here.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: Not with those houses behind it.

scenes.summary: The crew receives confirmation of Tamsin's detention while fitting the last community-made tiles to the flight article. Milo wants to abandon the upcoming launch window and go after her immediately. Arvin initially sees rescue and launch as competing deadlines until Lucia rejects the premise.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: We are not launching while she is in their truck.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: If we lose this window, separated basins lose the bridge for weeks.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: Then stop treating those as two missions.

scenes.summary: Lucia lays the detention convoy route over the Sky-Piercer's mobile launch route. The paths cross near a Tethergrid service transfer point shortly before the final launch corridor opens. The rescue, the movement of the launchpad and the launch itself can become one operation, but only if the rest of Public Sky runs without the crew.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: We pass within six kilometers of the transfer point.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: That is not an accident I trust.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: It is geography. We can use it.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: Then the communities run the network while we move.

scenes.summary: The finished Sky-Piercer dominates a mobile desert launch cradle: a large hand-built vehicle covered in small community-made ablative tiles, modular plumbing and visible access panels. Arvin, Milo and Lucia perform final checks while ordinary Public Sky maintenance crews deliver the last certified parts. The machine looks collective rather than improvised.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: Tile one ninety-eight came from a school maintenance shop.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: Does it pass the gauge?

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: Perfectly.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: Then it flies.

scenes.summary: In Tethergrid detention, Cyrus interviews Tamsin about who now controls Public Sky. She explains that community keys, local trip limits and ground-loop routes are deliberately divided. Cyrus keeps asking for the central authority until he understands there is no credential whose seizure would stop the system.
scenes.settingText: Tethergrid field detention and interview module — immaculate graphite-and-alloy interior, restrained corporate lighting, secure but non-theatrical furnishings and visible procedural controls.

dialogueInline.speaker: Cyrus
dialogueInline.text: Who can raise a basin limit?

dialogueInline.speaker: Tamsin
dialogueInline.text: The people sharing that basin, inside the physical floor.

dialogueInline.speaker: Cyrus
dialogueInline.text: Who can overrule them?

dialogueInline.speaker: Tamsin
dialogueInline.text: Nobody. That's why the console keeps telling you 'six keys.'

scenes.summary: Lucia converts the launch route into a precise rescue plan. Milo owns the launchpad timing and mechanical contingencies; Arvin owns flight readiness; Lucia owns the transfer-point intercept. Arvin does not micromanage the other two, and each plan has a clear abort condition.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: If the transport leaves the service road early, I abort the rescue and follow. You keep the launch alive.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: If the cradle loses steering, we stop before the storm, not inside it.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: And if flight readiness drops below margin, nobody talks me into a launch.

scenes.summary: Cyrus records a Tethergrid emergency statement warning that an unlicensed heavy launch through a contested corridor can endanger other orbital assets and ground populations. He insists on the real safety argument and refuses the board's request to describe the rocket as a weapon without evidence.

dialogueInline.speaker: Cyrus
dialogueInline.text: Call it a heavy unlicensed vehicle. That's enough.

dialogueInline.speaker: Cyrus
dialogueInline.text: Do not call it a weapon.

scenes.summary: A heavy unlicensed launch path crosses a restricted orbital corridor while uncertainty cones widen around storm-obscured tracking and ground exclusion zones.
scenes.settingText: Tethergrid emergency launch advisory — severe but technically grounded corridor graphics.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tetherwell Narrator
dialogueInline.text: A heavy launch vehicle does not become safe because its purpose is sympathetic. Shared sky requires verified trajectories, accountable operators and reliable exclusion zones.

scenes.summary: Dryline overlays the emergency warning with a month of Public Sky allocation data. The distributed communities are drawing less total water than their previous Tetherwell contracts allowed while maintaining emergency reserves. The report does not make the launch legal; it makes the monopoly argument harder to hide inside the safety argument.
Community draw bars remain below their prior contracted Tetherwell volumes while reserve bands stay visible. The launch-safety warning remains on screen beside the separate water-allocation record.
scenes.settingText: The Dryline Report — month-long comparison of Public Sky draw, reserve and trip data against former Tetherwell allocations.

dialogueInline.speaker: Dryline Reporter
dialogueInline.text: The launch dispute is real. It is also separate from the water dispute. Public Sky communities used less water this month than their old contracts permitted.

scenes.summary: Before the crew departs, community delegates take control of the regional allocation board without Arvin, Milo or Lucia in the room. Tamsin's rotated keys remain valid despite her detention. The network continues making ordinary decisions while its founders are busy with the most dramatic machine they have ever built.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: If anybody needs us for routine allocation today, we have already failed.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: Nobody has called in forty minutes.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: Try not to sound hurt.

scenes.summary: The mobile Sky-Piercer cradle enters a rising Mojave sandstorm to reduce long-range optical tracking during the final approach to the launch site. The storm is concealment with a cost: visibility drops, grit loads the steering joints and every unsecured panel becomes a hazard. Milo slows the convoy rather than racing the weather.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: We wanted cover. We got abrasive darkness.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: Speed limit?

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: Half what we planned.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: Then we arrive later and intact.

scenes.summary: At the Tethergrid service transfer point, Lucia intercepts Tamsin's transport by triggering a legitimate maintenance closure on the storm-damaged road and forcing the convoy into a low-speed inspection lane. When the vehicle stops, Lucia disables its external door lock and Tamsin opens the interior release herself. No nearby community becomes a battlefield.
scenes.settingText: Mojave service road and Tethergrid transport corridor — hard-packed desert road, sparse utility structures, long visibility and disciplined vehicle spacing.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: Door is yours.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tamsin
dialogueInline.text: About time.
