dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: You had the harder half.

scenes.summary: Cyrus sees the detention transport drop off the network and immediately understands that the launch route and rescue route are the same operation. He takes an interceptor toward the mobile cradle but orders the remaining units to stay off community roads where the storm has reduced civilian visibility.

dialogueInline.speaker: Cyrus
dialogueInline.text: They tied the rescue to the launch.

dialogueInline.speaker: Cyrus
dialogueInline.text: Keep the pursuit on the service corridor. No blind crossings through settlements.

scenes.summary: A steering actuator on the mobile cradle fills with grit and begins binding. Milo stops the convoy inside the storm, opens the protected access panel and replaces the actuator seal while ground-loop relays feed him weather and road updates from communities ahead. The network helps move the rocket without being commanded by the rocket crew.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: I need eight minutes and a road report that is newer than my problem.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tamsin
dialogueInline.text: Three communities are already passing you one.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: See? Infrastructure.

scenes.summary: At the launch site, Cyrus reaches Arvin before fueling is complete. He has the authority and personnel to impound the vehicle, but a board command arrives ordering immediate remote lockout of every nonpaying Tetherwell community during the emergency. The order would cut functioning pumps regardless of each basin's actual reserve state.

dialogueInline.speaker: Cyrus
dialogueInline.text: Stand down the vehicle.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: You can stop the launch. You still haven't answered the lockout.

dialogueInline.speaker: Cyrus
dialogueInline.text: The lockout is a separate order.

scenes.summary: Cyrus compares the board lockout command with live Public Sky basin data that shows compliant draw, intact reserves and local trip protection. He does not join Launch-Shop or forgive the illegal launch. He refuses to execute a blanket water shutoff that has no conservation basis and tells the board he will enforce flight safety separately from subscription collection.

dialogueInline.speaker: Cyrus
dialogueInline.text: I will enforce the corridor rules.

dialogueInline.speaker: Cyrus
dialogueInline.text: I will not enforce account lockouts as safety orders.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: There it is.

dialogueInline.speaker: Cyrus
dialogueInline.text: It still does not make your rocket legal.

scenes.summary: The board bypasses Cyrus and orders an automated kinetic intercept against the launch corridor. Cyrus blocks the firing authorization because storm-obscured tracking cannot guarantee a safe exclusion zone around the mobile site. His refusal protects public safety, not Launch-Shop allegiance, but it removes the immediate strike.

dialogueInline.speaker: Cyrus
dialogueInline.text: Tracking confidence below release. Denied.

dialogueInline.speaker: Cyrus
dialogueInline.text: Find me a clean shot or stand down.

scenes.summary: During final pressurization, one booster feed begins oscillating outside the validated range. Arvin calls for the modular booster to be isolated and abandoned rather than forcing it through the countdown. The Sky-Piercer loses performance margin but remains inside the minimum flight envelope the crew established before the crisis.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: Booster three is hunting.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: Isolate three.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: We lose eight percent.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: We keep the vehicle. Controlled loss.

scenes.summary: The Sky-Piercer launches through the sandstorm on the remaining boosters. Its community-made ablative tiles char and shed heat exactly as the second burn test predicted. Ground-loop relays hand off flight and allocation updates while the vehicle climbs beyond the closed local corridor toward a higher temporary bridge.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: Shield temperature is inside profile.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: Tracking?

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: Ugly and sufficient.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: Keep the climb.

scenes.summary: Tamsin joins the community allocation board from the launch site only long enough to confirm her rotated authority is no longer special. Delegates in separate communities approve the first cross-basin schedule carried by the new bridge without asking Launch-Shop to choose winners.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tamsin
dialogueInline.text: My key is one of six now.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: Good.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tamsin
dialogueInline.text: You are getting very comfortable with that word.

scenes.summary: Cyrus watches the new bridge appear on a Tethergrid basin map beside multiple ground loops, local trip modules and independent community keys. There is no command center to seize and no single uplink whose loss would restore Tetherwell's exclusive control. Tethergrid still exists, conservation still matters, and the monopoly no longer defines the only workable network.

dialogueInline.speaker: Cyrus
dialogueInline.text: There is no center.

dialogueInline.speaker: Cyrus
dialogueInline.text: That was the objective.

scenes.summary: After sunrise, Arvin, Milo and Lucia sit beside the cooling mobile cradle while ordinary maintenance crews service it for whatever comes next. On a community board in the distance, the next draw limits and relay window are already posted by people the crew never met. Milo asks who gets the next orbital window. Arvin tells him to ask the network that now knows how to answer without them.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: Who gets the next window?

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: Ask them.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: That may be the first time you built something correctly by leaving yourself out of it.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: I had help.

scenes.summary: In a quiet Tethergrid office, Cyrus formally separates basin-safety enforcement from account-status lockouts in the orders under his authority, knowing the board can challenge or reverse him. The institutional fight is not over, but stewardship and subscription collection are no longer treated as identical in his command chain.

dialogueInline.speaker: Cyrus
dialogueInline.text: Safety limits remain. Account lockouts require separate authority.

dialogueInline.speaker: Cyrus
dialogueInline.text: Put my name on it.

scenes.summary: The final image returns to the Mojave at night. A modest community relay blinks beside a working pump while the Sky-Piercer's temporary bridge crosses overhead among other independent paths. Water remains scarce, equipment still needs limits, and the sky is no longer singularly controllable.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tamsin
dialogueInline.text: Reserve is holding.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: Then we do not touch it.
